demonstration: supplied recovery image (recovery@3) with its separate authorization: decision=recovery
derived counterfactual (recovery-unauthorized@3) with the authorization removed: decision=reject-rollback
recoveryAuthorization.conclusion: Recovery is a separately authorized destination. The same signed, non-corrupt, correctly bound image enters recovery only when the authorization is present; without it the protected rollback state rejects it, so a valid signature alone does not open the recovery path.

supportedByThisFixture: the board-observed current image (current@7) boots, recorded on the serial boot log
the production key-hash fuse record is read on the board and matches the configured productionKeyHash (prod-key-hash-2026)
unsigned, corrupt and wrong-product fixtures are rejected before execution in the state machine
the signed older image is rejected as a rollback at every power-cut step
every supplied power-cut transition recovers to an authenticated current, candidate or authorized-recovery slot
recovery requires the separate authorization: removing it turns the same signed recovery image into a rollback rejection
notEstablished: debug lock and effective debug privilege: the corpus records emulator.debugLockProof=false and boot-config debugFuseObserved=false
physical fuse enforcement and resistance to physical secret extraction: the corpus records emulator.physicalFuseProof=false
invasive or fault-injection resistance: not modeled by the simulator
production lock register semantics: the register value is read on the board, but what it enforces is outside this fixture
claims.claimBoundary: This artifact shows the boot, rollback, recovery and power-cut state machine. Fuse state, debug lock, physical secret extraction resistance and power-fail behaviour on real silicon are outside what a simulator can show.

limits: The simulator models decisions and slot selection, not flash wear, bit-rot or a partially erased slot: the pre-commit recovery rule is the configured fail-safe, not a measurement.
Only the supplied key-hash fuse record is board-observed; the corpus marks physicalFuseProof and debugLockProof as unavailable in the emulator.
Digests are content digests of the corpus image records, not measurements of flash contents on hardware.
The recovery-authorization counterfactual and the update candidates are derived fixtures: they are labelled as such and are not present in evidence/device-corpus.json.
No fleet, credential or communication behaviour is asserted here: those surfaces have no observation in this fixture.
